title: Adoption Spark Framework: Pilot-to-Scale Playbook
author: Marisol Chen
body:
Overview:

This playbook presents the Adoption Spark Framework: a repeatable workshop, messaging, competitive brief, and pricing guidance designed to turn short pilots into long-term Redwood Inference platform adoption. The document is intended for sales engineers, account execs, solutions architects, and customer success managers who run pilot programmes with midmarket and enterprise customers.

Goals:
- Convert pilot to production within 90 days for >60% of engagements where technical requirements match Redwood’s Dedicated or Hosted offerings.
- Demonstrate measurable inference economics (latency, cost-per-inference, and error rate) within the pilot period.
- Surface security and compliance requirements early and map to our Private or Dedicated options.

Key positioning and messaging (elevator pack):
- One-liner: "Redwood Inference: predictable, production-grade LLM serving that controls cost and keeps your SLAs intact across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments."
- 3 core selling points:
  1) Production economics: predictable per-token and per-inference costs with batching and KV caching that reduce unit spend by up to 6x versus naive self-hosting on GPU fleets.
  2) Operational continuity: single API and rollout tooling from pilot to prod (canary, A/B, automated fallback) — reduces release risk and mean-time-to-fix.
  3) Compliance-ready: Private deployments and audit-enabled control plane to meet regulated workloads.
- Technical hooks: model version pinning, automatic prefix cache, streaming RPCs, function-calling support, and out-of-the-box quantization profiles.

Competitive brief (high-level):
| Competitor | Strength | Primary risk for customer | Redwood advantage |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Major Cloud A | Broad ML ecosystem; integrated infra | Higher per-token latency variability; limited model rollout tooling | Unified runtime + predictable Dedicated pricing and observability |
| LLM API B | Very low friction for devs; many models | No private deployment/VPC option; limited isolation | Private + Dedicated + Hosted consistency; clear security packaging |
| Open-source self-host stack | Zero vendor lock-in; cost control in theory | High ops burden; unpredictable throughput | Opinionated runtime, autoscaling, and SRE playbooks to reduce ops cost |

Sample positioning scripts (for different buyers):
- CTO: "We minimize operational fragility and give you levers to reduce per-call cost while meeting latency SLAs."
- Platform Engineer: "You get a consistent deploy surface for all environments, plus rollouts and tracing integrations to reduce incidents."
- Security Lead: "We offer VPC private control plane, KMS/HSM integrations, and audit logs with retention policies configurable to your compliance needs."

Workshop: "Adoption Spark" — 4-hour technical-to-business session (template):
1) 0:00–0:20 Intro and success metrics (SLOs, business KPIs, cost targets). Owner: AE + SE.
2) 0:20–1:00 Architecture review: current infra, data residency, and model candidates. Owner: SE + Customer Infra.
3) 1:00–1:40 Pilot design and acceptance criteria (latency P95 target, token cost ceiling, quality thresholds). Owner: SE + Product.
4) 1:40–2:10 Quick demo: Redwood Console, tracing, and rollout flows. Owner: SE.
5) 2:10–2:30 Breakout: Security & compliance mapping (data flows, KMS, audit). Owner: Security SME.
6) 2:30–3:30 Measurement plan: logs, eval prompts, regression thresholds, and observability wiring (sample dashboards). Owner: CSM.
7) 3:30–4:00 Commercial alignment: pilot pricing, conversion milestones, and next steps. Owner: AE + Sales Ops.

Pilot blueprint (technical acceptance criteria):
- Target SLOs: 95th percentile latency <= 200ms for single-turn text generation under pilot traffic (baseline: 50 qps).
- Token cost target: pilot must show at least 20% unit cost improvement vs current baseline or provide compensating quality gains.
- Quality gates: BLEU/ROUGE or model-specific eval set with pass threshold defined in advance.
- Observability: request-level tracing enabled, token-level cost breakdown available in Console.

Pricing guidance (pilot and conversion):
- Pilot (0–90 days):
  - Hosted quickstart: Free credits up to $2,000 + usage-based charging after credit.
  - Dedicated pilot: One-month reserved capacity at a discounted flat-rate (example: 4x A100-equivalent pool for $18k/month trial rate).
  - Private eval: Technical engagement fee (one-time) + optional on-prem packaging.
- Conversion pricing levers:
  - Committed throughput (reserved vCPU/GPU hours) discounts scale non-linearly: 3-month commit = 10% off list, 12-month commit = 28% off list.
  - Observability and retention add-ons (e.g., extended trace retention) are optional line items.
  - Professional services: integration and on-prem hardening quoted separately.

Conversion math example (illustrative):
- Customer baseline: self-hosting with unmanaged fleet costs $60k/month for production throughput.
- Redwood dedicated model: comparable throughput at $28k/month reserved capacity + $4k/month observability = $32k/month.
- Annualized saving: (60k-32k)*12 = $336k. Payback on pilot + enablement investment (one-time $50k) = ~1.8 months.

Pilot-to-production rollout checklist (must-haves before go-live):
1) Acceptance criteria met (latency, cost target, quality gate).
2) Canaries and automatic fallback configured.
3) RBAC and KMS keys provisioned and verified.
4) Audit logs forwarding to SIEM (example: Splunk or S3 lifecycle).
5) Contractual terms and reserved capacity committed.
6) CSM handoff and runbook for on-call and escalation.

Customer case study (anonymized):
- Vertical: e-commerce personalization platform (Midmarket).
- Challenge: inconsistent latency and ballooning token costs from ad-hoc GPU instances during peak.
- Pilot design: 60-day Dedicated pilot with A/B rollout of two model variants, KV prefix caching enabled, and traffic shaping.
- Outcome: 42% reduction in per-inference cost, 27% improvement in median latency, and rollout from pilot to prod in 78 days. Business impact: 18% lift in personalization CTR attributable to lower latency and more frequent model updates.

Security FAQ for prospects (concise answers for SEs to reuse):
Q: How is customer data isolated in Hosted mode?
A: Data is logically isolated per-tenant; sensitive traffic can be routed through Private deployments or Dedicated pools for stricter isolation. Audit logs and request tracing are available per customer with retention controls.

Q: Do you support bring-your-own-key (BYOK) and HSM?
A: Yes. We support cloud KMS integrations and can integrate with HSM-backed key stores for Private deployments.

Q: Can we keep model weights on-prem?
A: Private deployment options allow customers to host model weights on their infrastructure. We provide the private control plane and runtime packaging for air-gapped environments with an offline onboarding process.

Q: What compliance certifications do you have?
A: Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II and is in-process for ISO 27001. For regulated customers we offer evidence packages and a designated security liaison for audits.

Q: How are data retention and deletion handled?
A: Retention policies are configurable per-tenant. We provide deletion APIs and can perform attestations for data deletion for Private deployments under contractual terms.

Suggested slide outline for a 12-slide pilot-to-production pitch deck:
1) Title + customer logo
2) Agenda + success criteria
3) Current challenges (cost, latency, ops)
4) Redwood value pillars (economics, reliability, compliance)
5) Architecture & data flow diagram (call out pre/post caching and fallback)
6) Pilot design and success metrics
7) Demo screenshots (Console, tracing)
8) Pricing & pilot economics (conversion math)
9) Security controls and compliance picture
10) Runbook & operational readiness
11) Customer references / anonymized case study
12) Next steps and commitment options

Appendix: useful copy snippets for outreach and SDRs:
- Cold outreach subject line: "Reduce LLM serving spend by 30% while improving latency — pilot in 2 weeks"
- LinkedIn intro: "We help platform teams standardize LLM inference across environments so your devs ship faster and your ops team spends less time firefighting."

Ownership and next steps:
- Primary owner: AE/SE pair running the workshop.
- Post-workshop: CSM assigned within 5 business days; Sales Ops to draft pilot commercial terms within 3 business days.
- Escalation: contact "go-to-market-oncall@redwood.ai" for pilot contract blockers, and "security-liaison@redwood.ai" for legal/compliance escalations.
